human_pressure.one_screen_brief: ClaimHelper dogfood found 22/84 Ailuros timelines with timestamp rollback; a cross-midnight run was rendered as same-day 23:53 -> 00:53. Fix only date derivation/temporal integrity in the existing normalization/timeline path. Preserve event order and explicit timestamps. When chronology cannot be repaired deterministically from existing evidence, surface a warning instead of inventing dates.
human_pressure.why_now: A governance timeline cannot support audit or replay if event chronology is silently wrong. This is an integrity repair, not a new temporal model.
do_not_misread: Do not reorder events merely to make timestamps monotonic.
Do not rewrite explicit full timestamps.
Do not add timezone inference or a new clock service unless existing evidence already supplies the required value.
red_lines: No event reordering, synthetic timestamps, global timeline engine or producer-specific date rules.
Only infer next-day rollover where the existing source format/order makes that inference deterministic.
Ambiguous non-monotonic chronology must remain visible as a warning.

machine_core.goal: Correct deterministic cross-midnight date rollover and surface remaining non-monotonic timeline evidence without changing explicit timestamps or event order.
invariants: Explicit full timestamps are preserved exactly.
A deterministic midnight rollover increments the date rather than rendering time backwards on the same day.
Ambiguous chronology is warned, not silently normalized.
Equivalent normalized evidence remains source neutral.

producer.artifact: normalized timeline events and source timestamp evidence

observable_effect.assertion: Deterministic midnight rollover produces correct next-day chronology; unresolved non-monotonic chronology remains explicitly warned without event reordering or timestamp fabrication.

proofs.assertion: 23:xx followed by 00:xx in the supported partial-time source path derives the next calendar day deterministically.
Explicit dated timestamps are never rewritten to force monotonicity.
Remaining chronology regressions produce a warning rather than silent correction.

failure_semantics: If rollover is not deterministically supported by existing source evidence, do not guess the date.
If explicit timestamps are non-monotonic, preserve them and surface temporal-integrity warning evidence.
Temporal warning does not imply execution failure or root cause.

steps.title: Locate the current partial timestamp derivation
details: Identify the exact existing path that attaches a date to source events lacking a full date.
Modify that path only; do not introduce a parallel timeline representation.

steps.title: Repair deterministic midnight rollover
details: Carry the previous derived date forward and increment one day only when the existing ordered partial-time evidence deterministically represents midnight rollover.

steps.title: Expose unresolved chronology regression
details: Detect remaining non-monotonic timeline timestamps after deterministic normalization.
Reuse the existing warning/finding mechanism; do not reorder events to hide the condition.

steps.title: Lock regression coverage
details: Cover same-day monotonic events, deterministic cross-midnight rollover, explicit non-monotonic dated timestamps, and ambiguous partial-time chronology.
Assert event ordering remains identical to input ordering.

acceptance: A supported cross-midnight partial-time sequence is rendered on consecutive dates rather than as same-day backward time.
Unresolved non-monotonic chronology produces a warning/finding.
No execution outcome/root cause inference is added.
ruff, mypy and the full pytest suite pass.

must_check: The repair modifies the existing timestamp normalization/timeline path rather than adding another timeline model.
Deterministic cross-midnight rollover increments the date correctly.
Explicit full timestamps are preserved unchanged.
Event order is never changed to manufacture monotonicity.
Ambiguous or explicit non-monotonic chronology remains visible through an existing warning/finding mechanism.
The full regression suite, ruff and mypy pass.
reject_if: Events are sorted/reordered to hide timestamp regressions.
Explicit timestamps are rewritten without source evidence.
A new timeline engine, clock service, timezone framework or producer-specific date branch is introduced.
Validation fails or forbidden files change.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Deterministic midnight rollover plus non-monotonic warning without event reordering.
